reasons: CI installs with these settings and runs lint, type checks and tests on every pull request.

terms.meaning: A fast Python package installer and runner used by CI.
A Python linter that checks style and common mistakes.
A type checker for Python code.
Lets test functions run code that waits for work without blocking.

used_by: All Python code in the repository

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: All project settings
sections.what: Holds the runtime and development packages, the linter rules, strict type checking, and test options, including a warning that is turned into an error.
sections.why: The comments explain the warning rule and the test path setting. Reasons for the other choices are not stated in the file.
sections.watch_out: The type-checker override and the test path setting break easily when files move.

summary: Declares the Python project: its name, minimum Python version, runtime libraries, development tools, and the settings for the linter, type checker and tests.
purpose: Lets anyone install the same libraries and run the same checks, and sets how strict each check is.
why: Some settings explain themselves in comments, such as the warning rule and the test path setting. Most other choices have no stated reason in the file.
how: 1. Declares the runtime packages and a minimum Python version of 3.12. 2. Declares the development packages. 3. Sets the linter to a 100 character line length and a set of rule groups. 4. Sets the type checker to strict mode. 5. Sets the test runner to async mode, the tests folder, and treats one named warning as an error.
inputs: The package index and the project's Python code.
outputs: An installable environment, and settings used by ruff, mypy and pytest.
risks: Lower bounds only allow newer major versions to install, which can break code. The warning-as-error rule applies only under test. One type-checker override names a bare module called run.
debug: If installs fail, check the Python version first. If a check reports unexpected rules, find the matching table in this file. A failure on the warning rule means a first-party warning was raised during tests.
